exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, elective cesarean section, emergency cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 759 Chinese women aged 20-45 years who gave birth at The Seventh Hospital of the Southern Medical University between October 2019 and June 2021.
finding: Cesarean section (CS) was identified as an independent risk factor for postpartum PTSD in Chinese women.
mod_finding: Women with elective CS (RR = 1.70) and emergency CS (RR = 1.95) had an increased risk of developing postpartum PTSD compared with women with vaginal delivery.
